problem.title: Thread Pool Queue Sizing Masking SRE Alert Metrics Until Collapse
problem.prompt: Microservice with a thread pool queue size of 50,000 tasks.
requirements: Operational Invariant: "Deep in-memory queues hide latency degradation; keep queues shallow and alert aggressively on Queue Wait Time."
Production Hardening: Keep in-memory queues small (<=100 items), monitor Queue Wait Time and Queue Depth in real-time, and trigger high-priority alerts when Queue Wait Time exceeds 50ms.
Prevent cascading failure by isolating downstream degradation at the ingress boundary.
constraints: Incident Scenario Baseline: Microservice with a thread pool queue size of 50,000 tasks.
Failure Cascade Path: Burst → Pool Saturated → Queue Bloat (10k) → STW GC → 💥 504 Timeouts
Sub-millisecond rejection / shed latency for overloaded requests

stages.learnerPrompt: What catastrophic failure physics occur when capacity limits or downstream dependencies degrade under peak load?

referenceMaterial.summary: Failure physics analysis: Burst → Pool Saturated → Queue Bloat (10k) → STW GC → 💥 504 Timeouts.
failureModes: Cascading Failure: When downstream services slow down, incoming requests queue silently in the 50,000-slot queue. SRE alerts monitor error rates (0%) and thread count (100%), but not queue wait time. By the time requests timeout, 50,000 requests are stuck, and the system collapses with no early warning.
Breakdown Chain: Burst → Pool Saturated → Queue Bloat (10k) → STW GC → 💥 504 Timeouts
Shedding Failure: Without fast rejection at the boundary, queued dead work triggers multi-second GC pauses, CPU thrashing, and cascading 504 Gateway Timeouts.

stages.learnerPrompt: How does the system enforce physical resource boundaries under sudden downstream latency brownouts?

referenceMaterial.summary: Senior Staff SRE Interview challenge and architectural invariant verification.
tradeOffs: Architectural Invariant: "Deep in-memory queues hide latency degradation; keep queues shallow and alert aggressively on Queue Wait Time."
Physical Resource Boundary: Dynamic admission control ensures worker threads never buffer dead requests during downstream brownouts.
approachSteps: 1. Track real-time latency gradients and inflight concurrency.
2. Reject excess traffic at the ingress boundary within <0.1ms.
3. Monitor P99 latency and verify autonomous recovery when downstream pressure subsides.
